newsitem.title: USA: Crude prices gain in U.S., June grade barrels even.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices gain in U.S., June grade barrels even.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gained late Wednesday on active technical buying in NYMEX futures markets, while June grade barrels attracted scant attention.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged 25 cents higher at $21.75-85 a barrel, and also carried a 20-23 cents premium to the cash June WTI benchmark.
Cash traders in the U.S. Gulf said the focus of market attention was on the expectation for a Thursday announcement on how much foreign crude was delivered against June paper contracts.

Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) have moved above a 20 cents premium on refiner buying. EFPs act as protection from having to take delivery of physical foreign barrels, allowing the EFP buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for a physical position.
In the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James declined some five cents to trade at eight and nine cents below June benchmark.
Midland/WTI sold at 41 and 42 cents under WTI.
Traders said West Texas Sour/Midland was steady at $1.50 under benchmark, with Eugene Island pegged at the same levels.
June WTI/Cushing Postings was talked around $1.70-75.
